title: PSB Rc 96 (Ibulao) Rice Variety: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: PSB Rc 96 Rice Variety: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: PSB Rc 96 is an inbred rice for cool, elevated areas: about 136 days and 3.6 tonnes per hectare on average. See its pest ratings and grain quality.
excerpt: PSB Rc 96 is an inbred rice variety for cool, elevated areas, known locally as Ibulao. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 2001. IRRI bred it. It matures in about 136 days and averages 3.6 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 5.3 tonnes in trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for rice variety 96, or Rc 96, this is the one. The facts below come from sources that include PhilRice and its public seed database. So you can compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

blocks.text: How much does PSB Rc 96 yield?

On average it gives 3.6 tonnes per hectare. That is about 72 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits below the average of the 10 cool, elevated areas inbreds in PhilRice's list, which is 3.8 tonnes. But the top yield, 5.3 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 136 days from sowing to harvest. IRRI groups varieties of 100 to 120 days as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as medium duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow, as PalayCheck advises. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in PhilRice's tests: R resistant, MR moderately resistant, I intermediate, MS moderately susceptible, S susceptible. Some carry a second rating in brackets, as PhilRice lists them.

blocks.text: So scout early for [rice blast](/diseases/rice-blast), [bacterial leaf blight](/diseases/bacterial-leaf-blight), [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro), [green leafhopper](/pests/green-leafhopper). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

blocks.caption: Grain quality in PhilRice's seed database

blocks.text: Amylose decides how rice cooks. With high amylose, expect rice that is firm and dry, and it hardens as it cools. In fact, PhilRice notes that Filipino taste moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer. Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

It suits cool, elevated places such as the rice terraces of the Cordillera, where the nights stay cold. So use it where lowland varieties grow too slowly or set too few grains. PhilRice recommends it for the dry season and the wet season. You can plant it dry direct seeded, transplanted or wet direct seeded. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: What is the local name of PSB Rc 96?
items.a: It is known as Ibulao. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does PSB Rc 96 take to harvest?
items.a: About 136 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of PSB Rc 96?
items.a: PhilRice lists 3.6 tonnes per hectare on average, about 72 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 5.3 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.

items.q: In which season should I plant it?
items.a: PhilRice recommends it for the dry season and the wet season. Then pick the month with our planting calendar guide and the forecast for your town.
No, it is an inbred. So the seed you buy grows true, but certified seed still gives the best start, as PalayCheck advises.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In PhilRice's tests it was weak against rice blast, bacterial leaf blight, tungro, green leafhopper. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
